rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night’s retreat means that it has turned away; dabr and adbar can both mean departure. God swears by these signs to honor them and draw attention to divine wonders and the order of existence.
rows.anchor: والليل إذ أدبر: أي ولى، ويقال دبر وأدبر بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير ومجاهد وعطاء وابن يعمر وأبو جعفر وشيبة وأبو الزناد وقتادة وعمر بن العزيز والحسن وطلحة والنحويان والابنان وأبو بكر
rows.claim: This reading has idha, a future-time adverb, with dabr in the form dabr; the following reading of dawn is parallel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن الزبير ومجاهد وعطاء وابن يعمر وأبو جعفر

rows.speaker: ابن جبير والسلمي وابن سيرين والأعرج وزيد بن علي وأبو شيخ وابن محيصن ونافع وحمزة وحفص
rows.claim: This reading has idh, a past-time adverb, followed by the quadriliteral adbara.
rows.anchor: وابن جبير والسلمي والحسن: بخلاف عنهم وابن سيرين والأعرج وزيد بن علي وأبو شيخ وابن محيصن ونافع وحمزة وحفص: إذ ظرف زمان ماض، أدبر رباعيا

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو رزين وأبو رجاء وابن يعمر والسلمي وطلحة والأعمش ويونس بن عبيد ومطر
rows.claim: A further reading uses idha and the hamzated adbara; its parallel with idha asfara is reflected in the codices of ʿAbd Allah and Ubayy.
rows.anchor: إذا بالألف، أدبر بالهمز، وكذا هو في مصحف عبد الله وأبي، وهو مناسب لقوله: إذا أسفر

rows.speaker: يونس بن حبيب
rows.claim: Yunus distinguishes dabr as ‘ended’ from adbara as ‘turned away.’
rows.anchor: وقال يونس بن حبيب: دبر: انقضى، وأدبر: تولى

rows.speaker: قتادة والزمخشري
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the night’s dabr as its turning away; al-Zamakhshari treats dabr as adbara, parallel to qabila and aqbala.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: دبر الليل: ولى. وقال الزمخشري: ودبر بمعنى أدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the night’s departure as the day following it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من دبر الليل النهار: أخلفه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read asfara in the quadriliteral form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أسفر رباعيا

rows.speaker: ابن السميفع وعيسى بن الفضل
rows.claim: They read the triliteral safara, meaning that dawn removes darkness from its face.
rows.anchor: وابن السميفع وعيسى بن الفضل: سفر ثلاثيا، والمعنى: طرح الظلمة عن وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent antecedent of ‘it’ is Hell; alternatives are the warning or the affair of the Hereafter, or the Resurrection as an unmentioned antecedent.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الضمير في إنها عائد على النار. قيل: ويحتمل أن يكون للنذارة، وأمر الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One of the greatest means one of the immense calamities or punishments, with no equal; al-kubar is the plural of al-kubra.
rows.anchor: ومعنى إحدى الكبر: الدواهي الكبر، أي لا نظير لها

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: The cited rajaz line uses ‘one of the great calamities’ for a devastating misfortune.
rows.anchor: يا ابن المعلى نزلت إحدى الكبر ... داهية الدهر وصماء الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kubar is a plural of kubra with the feminine alif dropped; the book of Ibn ʿAtiyya instead says it is the plural of kabira, likely a copyist’s error.
rows.anchor: والكبر جمع الكبرى، طرحت ألف التأنيث في الجمع

rows.speaker: نصر بن عاصم وابن محيصن ووهب بن جرير عن ابن كثير
rows.claim: They omit the hamza in li-ihda; the omission is irregular, while the normal easing of this hamza is an intermediate pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نصر بن عاصم وابن محيصن ووهب بن جرير عن ابن كثير: بحذف الهمزة، وهو حذف لا ينقاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes the clause the answer to the oath; al-Zamakhshari alternatively makes it explain kalla, with the oath parenthetical for emphasis.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الجملة جواب للقسم. وقال الزمخشري: أو تعليل لكلا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Nadhiran may be a verbal noun meaning warning, used as a specification: one of the greatest calamities as a warning.
rows.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون مصدرا بمعنى الإنذار، كالنكير بمعنى الإنكار، فيكون تمييزا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats nadhiran as a verbal noun governed by an omitted verb: ‘warn as a warning.’
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو مصدر نصب بإضمار فعل، أي أنذر إنذارا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads nadhiran as an active participle in the circumstantial accusative from the pronoun in innaha.
rows.anchor: فقال الزجاج: حال من الضمير في إنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed attachments to the opening command, its later warning command, or al-kubar and its pronoun are unsound; Abu al-Baqaʾ’s circumstantial reading from the whole clause’s implied sense is acceptable.
rows.anchor: فهو بمعزل عن الصواب. قال أبو البقاء: والمختار أن يكون حالا مما دلت عليه الجملة

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas explains the missing feminine ending in nadhiran as a relational form meaning ‘possessing warning,’ referring to the fire.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: وحذفت الهاء من نذيرا، وإن كان للنار على معنى النسب

rows.speaker: علي بن سليمان والحسن وابن عطية
rows.claim: Ali b. Sulayman takes nadhiran as ‘I mean a warner’; al-Hasan reads it as ‘that I may warn,’ and Ibn ʿAtiyya says this makes it circumstantial from innaha or li-ihda.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن سليمان: أعني نذيرا. وقال الحسن: لأنذر

rows.speaker: أبو رزين وابن زيد
rows.claim: Abu Razin identifies the warner as God with an omitted verb; Ibn Zayd identifies him as Muhammad, likewise supplied by an omitted verb.
rows.anchor: أبو رزين: نذير هنا هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبي وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: They read nadhir in the nominative; it can predicate an omitted ‘it is’ for the fire or an omitted ‘he is’ for God or the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وابن أبي عبلة: نذير بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase liman is a replacement for al-bashar with the preposition repeated; the subject of yataqaddama is an implied pronoun referring to man.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن لمن بدل من البشر بإعادة الجار، وأن يتقدم منصوب بشاء ضمير يعود على من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative makes the subject of ‘wills’ an implied pronoun referring to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الفاعل ضمير يعود على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan takes the words as a threat like the choice of belief or unbelief in 18:29.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو وعيد، نحو قوله تعالى: فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya sees clarification that anyone can choose guidance and truth through sound reflection, but heedlessness and poor judgment keep people from it; he supports this with the next verse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هو بيان في النذارة وإعلام بأن كل أحد يسلك طريق الهدى والحق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses yataqaddama as a delayed subject and liman as its fronted predicate: whoever wishes may advance or lag, meaning hasten to good or fall behind.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أن يتقدم في موضع الرفع بالابتداء، ولمن شاء خبر مقدم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari’s interpretation is not readily apparent and requires ellipsis.
rows.anchor: انتهى، وهو معنى لا يتبادر إلى الذهن وفيه حذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations identify advancing with faith and lagging with unbelief; al-Suddi makes the contrast movement toward Hell or away toward Paradise.
rows.anchor: قيل: والتقدم: الإيمان، والتأخر: الكفر. وقال السدي: أن يتقدم إلى النار

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets advancing as undertaking commands and lagging as falling short of prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أن يتقدم إلى المأمورات، أو يتأخر عن المنهيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is general and applies to every person.
rows.anchor: والظاهر العموم في كل نفس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says every soul deserves punishment and God does not hold anyone of the people of Paradise in pledge.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كل نفس حقيق عليها العذاب، ولا يرتهن الله تعالى أحدا من أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahina means a pledge, not a passive participle; although it is originally passive in sense, the author prefers the form with feminine -a, contrasting the masculine rahin in 52:21.
rows.anchor: والذي أختاره أنها مما دخلت فيه التاء، وإن كان بمعنى مفعول في الأصل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the people of the right as angels, while Ali identifies them as Muslim children; on either view the exception is disconnected.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم الملائكة. وقال علي: هم أطفال المسلمين

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن كيسان
rows.claim: Hasan and Ibn Kaysan identify them as sincere Muslims, freed from the pledge because they fulfilled their duties, as in al-Dahhak’s earlier account.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وابن كيسان: هم المسلمون المخلصون، ليسوا بمرتهنين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the exception as connected: the people of the right released their own pledge through good deeds, as a debtor frees a pledge by payment.
rows.anchor: فإنهم فكوا عنه رقابهم بما أطابوه من كسبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatasaʾalun can mean that the people of the right ask each other, or that they ask others about absent acquaintances; the likeliest ellipsis is that they ask the criminals what brought them to Hell.
rows.anchor: والأقرب أن يكون التقدير: يتساءلون عن المجرمين قائلين لهم بعد التساؤل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the mismatch by supplying an omitted exchange: the people ask what happened, and the respondents recount asking the criminals why they entered Hell.
rows.anchor: لأن المسئولين يلقون إلى السائلين ما جرى بينهم وبين المجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls al-Zamakhshari’s account strained; the likelier reading makes the mutual questioners ask the criminals directly, with an implied saying.
rows.anchor: انتهى، وفيه تعسف. والأظهر أن السائلين هم المتسائلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question is rebuke and humiliation; the questioners already know what brought the criminals to Hell.
rows.anchor: وسؤالهم سؤال توبيخ لهم وتحقير، وإلا فهم عالمون ما الذي أدخلهم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals first lacked the Muslim practices of prayer and almsgiving, then moved to the greater sin of disbelief and denial of Judgment, echoing 90:11 and 90:17.
rows.anchor: لم يكونوا متصفين بخصائل الإسلام من إقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة، ثم ارتقوا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya interprets certainty as the truth they denied: return to God and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: واليقين عندي صحة ما كانوا يكذبون من الرجوع إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes commonly take certainty here as death, but the author objects that a living unbeliever already knows death is certain.
rows.anchor: وقال المفسرون: اليقين: الموت، وذلك عندي هنا متعقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here certainty is what unbelievers denied in worldly life and only recognized after death; ‘certainty’ means death in 15:99 instead.
rows.anchor: وإنما اليقين الذي عنوا في هذه الآية الشيء الذي كانوا يكذبون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse negates any intercession for them, rather than allowing intercession but saying it fails; its exclusive wording implies that other intercessions can benefit, as reports affirm.
rows.anchor: وإنما المعنى نفي الشفاعة فانتفى النفع

rows.speaker: الجمهور وابن جبير
rows.claim: The majority read suhufan with both letters rounded; Ibn Jubayr reads both with sukun and uses the lighter form of munashshara.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: صحفا بضم الصاد والحاء، منشرة مشددا وابن جبير: بإسكانها منشرة مخففا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munashshara likens spreading a page to God reviving the dead; for the dead one says God revived him and he lived.
rows.anchor: شبه نشر الصحيفة بإنشار الله الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes their demand for scriptures and shows the real reason for turning from the reminder: they do not fear the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: كلا: ردع عن إرادتهم تلك وزجر لهم عن اقتراح الآيات، بل لا يخافون الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads the verb ‘fear’ in the second person, as a shift to direct address.
rows.anchor: وأبو حيوة: بتاء الخطاب التفاتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla also rebukes their neglect of the reminder; the verse calls itself a reminder, since tadhkira means remembrance.
rows.anchor: كلا: ردع عن إعراضهم عن التذكرة، إنه تذكرة فمن شاء ذكره

rows.speaker: نافع وسلام ويعقوب وأبو جعفر والأعمش وطلحة وعيسى والأعرج وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: Several readings vary whether the reminder and remembering verbs address the listener, use third person, or assimilate the letters.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وسلام ويعقوب: تذكرة بتاء الخطاب ساكنة الذال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is worthy both of being feared and of forgiving.
rows.anchor: هو أهل التقوى: أي أهل أن يتقى ويخاف، وأهل أن يغفر

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet explaining that God alone deserves worshipful fear; whoever avoids associating another deity with Him is forgiven.
rows.anchor: أنا أهل أن أتقى، فلا يجعل يتقى إله غيري، ومن اتقى أن يجعل معي إلها غيري فأنا أغفر له

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets remembering only if God wills as God compelling remembrance, since hearts are sealed and they will not believe by choice.
rows.anchor: يعني: إلا أن يقسرهم على الذكر ويلجئهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barqa with kasra means to be terrified and stunned, from looking at lightning until the eye is dazed; the cited poetry illustrates the sense.
rows.anchor: برق بكسر الراء: فزع ودهش، وأصله من برق الرجل، إذا نظر إلى البرق فدهش بصره

rows.speaker: الأعشى وذو الرمة
rows.claim: The poems of al-Aʿsha and Dhu al-Rumma illustrate the eye’s dazed or flashing state associated with barq.
rows.anchor: وكنت أرى في وجه مية لمحة ... فأبرق مغشيا علي مكانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barqa with fatha means the eye split open or flashed from staring, from the root for shining.
rows.anchor: وبرق بفتح الراء: شق بصره، وهو من البريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan and follows the previous surah’s warnings about the Hereafter by detailing the Resurrection and its conditions; the oath honors the awesome Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية. ومناسبتها لما قبلها: أن في آخر ما قبلها قوله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan takes la as a negation: God denies swearing by the reproachful soul while swearing by the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قيل: لا نافية، نفى أن يقسم بالنفس اللوامة وأقسم بيوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand God to swear by both the Resurrection and the reproachful soul.
rows.anchor: والجمهور: على أن الله أقسم بالأمرين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan calls the self that reproaches its owner for neglected obedience praiseworthy, which explains the oath by it.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: هي التي تلوم صاحبها في ترك الطاعة ونحوها، فهي على هذا ممدوحة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid says this soul regrets missed opportunities, evil deeds, and failing to do more good.
rows.anchor: وروي نحوه عن ابن عباس وعن مجاهد، تلوم على ما فات وتندم على الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is a God-fearing soul that reproaches other souls at the Resurrection for falling short in piety.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النفس المتقية التي تلوم النفوس في يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: They identify it as the sinful, wretched soul that blames itself for missing worldly effort and pleasures, making it blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: هي الفاجرة الخشعة اللوامة لصاحبها على ما فاته من سعي الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nafs al-lawwama is either a generic class described by this quality or, in another view, one particular soul: Adam’s, continually reproaching him for leaving Paradise.
rows.anchor: والنفس اللوامة: اسم جنس بهذا الوصف. وقيل: هي نفس معينة، وهي نفس آدم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says every intermediate soul reproaches itself both for neglected obedience and missed desires; a tranquil soul becomes purified.
rows.anchor: وكل نفس متوسطة ليست بمطمئنة ولا أمارة بالسوء فإنها لوامة في الطرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oaths correspond because the soul’s happiness or misery becomes manifest on the Day of Resurrection; the oath’s omitted answer is that people will be raised.
rows.anchor: والمناسبة بين القسمين من حيث أحوال النفس من سعادتها وشقاوتها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks whether la before an oath can reinforce a negative omitted answer, as in ‘I swear by the Day of Resurrection: you are not left aimless.’
rows.anchor: وقدرت المقسم عليه المحذوف هاهنا منفيا، نحو قولك: لا أقسم بيوم القيامة، لا تتركون سدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari’s account works only if the wording is restricted to negation; Qur’anic oath examples instead pair la uqsimu with positive answers.
rows.anchor: ولكنه لم يقسم. ألا ترى كيف لقى لا أقسم بهذا البلد بقوله: لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والنحاس
rows.claim: They take the oath’s answer to be ‘you will surely be resurrected,’ indicated by ‘Does man think?’
rows.anchor: وجواب القسم ما دل عليه قوله: أيحسب الإنسان ألن نجمع عظامه، وهو لتبعثن

rows.speaker: الحسن وآخرون
rows.claim: The author dismisses proposals that the answer is ‘yes, able,’ that la negates both oaths, or that an unspoken question to the listener supplies the syntax.
rows.anchor: وقول من قال جواب القسم هو: أيحسب الإنسان. وما روي عن الحسن أن الجواب: بلى قادرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human in this passage is the unbeliever who denies resurrection.
rows.anchor: والإنسان هنا الكافر المكذب بالبعث

rows.speaker: عدي بن ربيعة
rows.claim: A report says ʿAdi b. Rabiʿa asked Muhammad when the Resurrection would happen and denied that he would believe or that God could restore decayed bones; the verse then came down.
rows.anchor: روي أن عدي بن ربيعة قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Another account says the passage came down about Abu Jahl, who mocked the claim that God would gather scattered, decayed bones into a new creation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في أبي جهل، كان يقول: أيزعم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يجمع الله

rows.speaker: الجمهور وقتادة
rows.claim: The majority read ‘we gather’ in first person and ‘his bones’ as accusative; Qatada reads the verb passively and the bones nominatively.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: نجمع بنون، عظامه نصبا وقتادة: بالتاء مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bones stand for the whole person because they form the body’s frame; the question is a rebuke that reports the denier’s challenge to God’s power.
rows.anchor: وذكر العظام، وإن كان المعنى إعادة الإنسان وجمع أجزائه المتفرقة

rows.speaker: الجمهور وابن أبي عبلة وابن السميفع
rows.claim: The majority read qadirin in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase; Ibn Abi ʿAbla and Ibn al-Sumayfi read qadirun, ‘We are able.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قادرين بالنصب على الحال من الضمير الذي في الفعل المقدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
rows.claim: They explain ‘make his fingertips even’ as making the hand’s bones a single piece during earthly life, reducing its usefulness.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والجمهور: المعنى نجعلها في حياته هذه بضعة، أو عظما واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is God’s ability to reassemble even the most dispersed and finely divided fingertip bones at resurrection.
rows.anchor: والمعنى الأول هو الظاهر والمقصود من رصف الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal marks a transition to a new statement without cancelling the prior affirmation of God’s power to gather the bones.
rows.anchor: بل: إضراب، وهو انتقال من كلام إلى كلام من غير إبطال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers three possible ways to attach ‘rather man wishes’ to the preceding rhetorical question; the author considers them strained.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: بل يريد عطف على أيحسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence independently describes man as heedless of the afterlife and occupied with desires; the object of ‘wishes’ is omitted and supplied by the reason clause.
rows.anchor: بل المعنى: الإخبار عن الإنسان من غير إبطال لمضمون الجملة السابقة

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وعكرمة وابن جبير والضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: They say man wants to pursue desires and sins endlessly, indulging himself and repeatedly postponing repentance.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد والحسن وعكرمة وابن جبير والضحاك والسدي: معنى الآية: أن الإنسان إنما يريد شهواته

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi also says man wants to commit as much oppression as he can.
rows.anchor:
قال السدي أيضا:
ليظلم على قدر طاقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘before him’ apparently refers to man and denotes the remaining span of his life.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالضمير في أمامه عائد على الإنسان، وهو الظاهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas instead relates ‘before him’ to the Resurrection ahead of a person in time: man pursues desire and denial during his life without understanding his limited interval.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ما يقتضي أن الضمير عائد على يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question ‘When is the Resurrection?’ is asked mockingly, in denial and obstinate challenge.
rows.anchor: يسئل أيان يوم القيامة: أي متى يوم القيامة؟ سؤال استهزاء وتكذيب وتعنت

rows.speaker: الجمهور وزيد بن ثابت ونصر بن عاصم وغيرهم
rows.claim: Both barqa with kasra and barqa with fatha are read; Abu ʿUbayda associates the open vowel with splitting, and Ibn Ishaq with fear at death.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: برق بكسر الراء وزيد بن ثابت ونصر بن عاصم

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: Mujahid locates the eye’s state at death, while Hasan locates it on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: هذا عند الموت. وقال الحسن: هو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو السمال وأهل اللغة وثعلب
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal’s variant changes r to l and means opened; lexicographers disagree with al-Farraʾ, whom Thaʿlab says erred by glossing it as closed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال: بلق باللام عوض الراء، أي انفتح وانفرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The l/r substitution has parallels in Arabic word pairs, including nathara/nathala and wajara/wajila.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون اللام بدلا من الراء، فهما يتعاقبان في بعض الكلام

rows.speaker: الجمهور وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة ويزيد بن قطيب وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: The majority read the Moon’s eclipse actively; the others read the verb passively.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وخسف مبنيا للفاعل وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن أبي أويس
rows.claim: Some lexicographers treat khusuf and kusuf as synonyms; Ibn Abi Uways distinguishes partial loss of light as kusuf from total loss as khusuf.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة وجماعة من أهل اللغة: الخسوف والكسوف بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd b. Aslam says what one sent ahead from wealth benefits oneself, while what one leaves behind goes to the heir.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: بما قدم من ماله لنفسه، وبما أخر منه للوارث

rows.speaker: النخعي ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi and Mujahid interpret what was sent ahead and left behind as a person’s first and last deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال النخعي ومجاهد: بأول عمله وآخره

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the pair as obligatory duties performed and duties neglected.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: بما قدم من فرض وأخر من فرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording should be taken generally, encompassing all acts mentioned by exegetes and others they did not mention.
rows.anchor: والظاهر حمله على العموم، أي يخبره بكل ما قدم وكل ما أخر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes basira as a witness and treats its feminine ending as intensive.
rows.anchor:
بصيرة
: خبر عن الإنسان، أي شاهد، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says basira is like calling a person an example or proof.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: هو كقولك: فلان عبرة وحجة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ allows an omitted noun, ‘a seeing eye,’ as the subject, and cites poetry describing an intelligent person as having a seeing eye.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بصيرة مبتدأ محذوف الموصوف، أي عين بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers basira as an agent governed by the prepositional phrase, which functions as the predicate; the feminine ending is grammatical.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا نختار أن تكون بصيرة فاعلا بالجار والمجرور، وهو الخبر عن الإنسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the witness as a person’s limbs or the guardian angels.
rows.anchor: وتأول ابن عباس البصيرة بالجوارح أو الملائكة الحفظة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand maʿadhir as excuses; every excuse fails because the person himself is a clear witness against himself.
rows.anchor: والمعاذير عند الجمهور الأعذار، فالمعنى: لو جاء بكل معذرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls maʿadhir a collective noun rather than a broken plural; the author rejects this morphology and treats its form as a broken plural.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: قياس معذرة معاذر، فالمعاذير ليس بجمع معذرة

rows.speaker: السدي والضحاك والزجاج
rows.claim: They say maʿadhir means curtains in Yemeni speech: a person may hide behind a screen, but his own self still testifies.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي والضحاك: المعاذير: الستور بلغة اليمن، واحدها معذار

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited verse uses maʿadhir in the sense of curtains or coverings.
rows.anchor: ولكنها ضنت بمنزل ساعة ... علينا وأطت فوقها بالمعاذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes basira as the two scribes who record good and evil deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: البصيرة: الكاتبان يكتبان ما يكون من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If maʿadhir means excuses, ‘even if he offers them’ means that he speaks and presents his excuses; it may also mean surrendering or offering a proof.
rows.anchor:
معنى ولو ألقى
: أي نطق بمعاذيره وقالها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the person may submit an argument and excuse for himself.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: ولو أدلى بحجة وعذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean that people blame one another, as in the disbelievers’ statement ‘If not for you, we would have believed.’
rows.anchor: وقيل: ولو أحال بعضهم على بعض، كقوله تعالى: لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound, apparent account of the revelation’s occasion makes the command not to move the tongue a direct address to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الظاهر والمنصوص الصحيح في سبب النزول أنه خطاب للرسول

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal instead addresses the human whose deeds are being read from his record: he is told not to rush, since God will gather and recite them to him.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال: هو خطاب للإنسان المذكور في قوله: ينبؤا الإنسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says the Prophet struggled during revelation and moved his lips for fear of losing what was being revealed, so the verse came down.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري عن ابن عباس: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يعالج من التنزيل شدة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Prophet feared forgetting the Qur’an and reviewed it until the practice became burdensome.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: السبب أنه كان عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يخاف أن ينسى القرآن

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi attributes the command to the Prophet’s eagerness to deliver the message: he might speak before the revelation was complete.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: كان لحرصه عليه الصلاة والسلام على أداء الرسالة والاجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘in your chest’ refers to the Qur’an, and qurʾan here means its recitation; the cited poem also uses qurʾanan for reciting.
rows.anchor: والقرآن مصدر كالقراءة، قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes qurʾan as the Qur’an’s composition and collection in the Prophet’s chest, from the root meaning to collect.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وقرآنه: وتأليفه في صدرك، فهو مصدر من قرأت: أي جمعت

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘when We recite it’ refers to the angel who conveys the Qur’an; follow it first with your mind and attention, says Ibn ʿAbbas.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: فاتبع حلاله واجتنب حرامه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbas, and reports from Qatada and al-Dahhak, take following the recitation as obeying its commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا هو قتادة والضحاك: فاتبع في الأوامر والنواهي

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya has a nonstandard reading with qaf, ra, and ta open and no hamza or alif in the three occurrences; the author explains its altered morphology.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية: فإذا قرته فاتبع قرته، بفتح القاف والراء والتاء من غير همز

rows.speaker: قتادة وجماعة
rows.claim: They say God will explain and preserve the Qur’an for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة وجماعة: أن نبينه لك ونحفظكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the Prophet responsible for explaining it; Qatada also says the explanation distinguishes lawful from forbidden and general from specific.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أن تبينه أنت. وقال قتادة أيضا: أن نبين حلاله وحرامه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God preserves the Qur’an during the Prophet’s life and arranges its recitation on his tongue.
rows.anchor: وفي التحرير والتحبير قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says God establishes the Qur’an in the Prophet’s heart after collecting it for him.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: نثبته في قلبك بعد جمعه لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report explains its collection as Gabriel repeating the revelation to the Prophet until it settles in his chest.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جمعه بإعادة جبريل عليك مرة أخرى إلى أن يثبت في صدرك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the revelation is to be listened to or followed in its contents; Qatada specifies that its lawful is followed and its forbidden avoided.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا: فإذا يتلى عليك فاتبع ما فيه. وقال قتادة: فاتبع حلاله واجتنب حرامه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Prophet hurried to memorize while Gabriel recited, so he should listen with heart and ear, then study it; divine preservation removes fear of loss.
rows.anchor: فأمر بأن يستنصت له ملقيا إليه بقلبه وسمعه حتى يقضى إليه وحيه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the Prophet hurried both to memorize and ask about meaning; the command assures preservation and defers questions until recitation ends.
rows.anchor: ثم إن علينا بيانه: إذا أشكل عليك شيء من معانيه، كأنه كان يعجل في الحفظ

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi reports that early extremist Rafidis alleged the Qur’an was altered, using the supposed lack of connection between these verses and what precedes.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن قد غير وبدل وزيد فيه ونقص منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees a clear contrast: one man rejects resurrection and revelatory signs, while the Prophet eagerly learns, preserves, and presents God’s signs in hope of acceptance.
rows.anchor: ويظهر أن المناسبة بين هذه الآية وما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After addressing the Prophet, the discourse returns to the earlier denier, whose concern is perishable worldly gain rather than reward in an afterlife he rejects.
rows.anchor: رجع إلى حال الإنسان السابق ذكره المنكر البعث، وأن همه إنما هو في تحصيل حطام الدنيا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the verbs in direct address to the Quraysh unbelievers; kalla rebukes them for letting worldly desire overwhelm concern for the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون بتاء الخطاب، لكفار قريش

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies kalla as a rebuke.
rows.anchor: كلا ردع، وذكر في كتابه ما يوقف عليه فيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وقتادة والجحدري وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read both verbs in the third person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد والحسن وقتادة والجحدري وابن كثير وأبو عمرو: بياء الغيبة فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Faces’ refers to the whole person; nadhira is read either with a long or short first vowel.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالوجه عن الجملة. وقرأ الجمهور: ناضرة بألف، وزيد بن علي: نضرة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya parses ‘faces’ as an indefinite subject made definite enough by ‘that day,’ with nadhira as its predicate and ‘toward its Lord looking’ as a further predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عطية: وجوه رفع بالابتداء، وابتدأ بالنكرة لأنها تخصصت بقوله: يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A time adverb cannot adjectivally qualify a concrete noun; the indefinite subject is licensed by the passage’s descriptive detail, or nadhira can itself be an adjective.
rows.anchor: وليس يومئذ تخصيصا للنكرة، فيسوغ الابتداء بها، لأن ظرف الزمان لا يكون صفة للجثة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects literal vision of God because the definite object would imply exclusive looking; he reads the phrase as hopeful expectation of grace.
rows.anchor: فوجب حمله على معنى لا يصح معه الاختصاص، والذي يصح معه أن يكون من قول الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says Muʿtazilites supply an omitted noun such as mercy, reward, or dominion; this is an acceptable Arabic construction.
rows.anchor: ذهبوا، يعني المعتزلة، إلى أن المعنى إلى رحمة ربها ناظرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes ila a preposition attached to naẓira; a Muʿtazili alternative treats ila as a plural of blessing and naẓira as ‘awaiting.’
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن إلى في قوله: إلى ربها حرف جر يتعلق بناظرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax allows ‘faces’ as subject and basira as predicate, with tazunnu as a second predicate, or basira as adjective with tazunnu as predicate.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون وجوه مبتدأ خبره باسرة وتظن خبر بعد خبر

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib glosses faqira as a back-breaking calamity; Abu ʿUbayda derives it from branding a camel’s nose with fire.
rows.anchor: والفاقرة قال ابن المسيب قاصمة الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazunnu can mean certainty, strong belief, or expectation that a crushing calamity will be inflicted.
rows.anchor: وتظن بمعنى توقن أو يغلب على اعتقادها وتتوقع أن يفعل بها فاقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes preferring this world to the next and reminds hearers of death, which ends the immediate life; ‘when it reaches’ refers to the soul implied by context.
rows.anchor: كلا: ردع عن إيثار الدنيا على الآخرة وتذكير لهم بما يؤولون إليه من الموت

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Amshaj means mixed substances; Ibn al-Aʿrabi gives several forms for the word, and the author adduces poetry as evidence for its use.
rows.anchor: الأمشاج: الأخلاط، واحدها مشج بفتحتين، أو مشج كعدل، أو مشيج كشريف وأشراف

rows.speaker: رؤبة والهذلي والشماخ
rows.claim: The cited verses by Ruʾba, a Hudhali poet, and al-Shammakh attest the vocabulary of mixed substances.
rows.anchor: الأمشاج: الأخلاط، واحدها مشج بفتحتين، أو مشج كعدل، أو مشيج كشريف وأشراف، قاله ابن الأعرابي، وقال رؤبة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb mashaja means to mix; mashij and mamthunj likewise mean mixed, as the cited poem about a drink’s blend illustrates.
rows.anchor: ويقال: مشج يمشج مشجا إذا خلط، ومشيج: كخليط، وممثنوج: كمخلوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istatar means spread; Arabic also uses it for a crack spreading along a vessel, while al-Farraʾ glosses mustatir as elongated.
rows.anchor: استطار الشيء: انتشر، وتقول العرب: استطار الصدع في القارورة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ glosses mustatir as ‘long’ or ‘extended.’
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: مستطير: مستطيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qumturir and qamaṭir describe a harsh, severe day.
rows.anchor: ويقال: يوم قمطرير وقماطر واقمطر، فهو مقمطر إذا كان صعبا شديدا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains qumṭarir as a person living until his brows draw together, or as a camel raising its tail and gathering its flanks; he derives it from qutr with an extra m.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: القمطرير: الذي يعيش حتى يجتمع ما بين عينيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The etymology is disputed because most grammarians do not accept ifmaʿalla among verb patterns.
rows.anchor: واختلف في هذا الوزن، وأكثر النحاة لا يثبت افمعل في أوزان الأفعال

rows.speaker: الزمهرير
rows.claim: Zamharir means intense cold; Thaʿlab alternatively says it means the moon in the Tayyiʾ dialect.
rows.anchor: الزمهرير: أشد البرد، وقال ثعلب: هو القمر بلغة طي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qarura is a thin, clear drinking vessel, perhaps made of glass.
rows.anchor: القارورة: إناء رقيق صاف توضع فيه الأشربة، قيل: ويكون من الزجاج

rows.speaker: الدينوري
rows.claim: Al-Daynuri describes ginger as a root-spreading plant of Oman, eaten fresh, with the best brought from China; Arabs liked its sharp sensation in drink.
rows.anchor: قال الدينوري: نبت في أرض عمان عروق تسري وليس بشجر، يؤكل رطبا

rows.speaker: المسيب بن علس
rows.claim: Al-Musayyib b. ʿAlas uses ginger’s taste in a poem describing it with wine.
rows.anchor: وقال المسيب بن علس: وكأن طعم الزنجبيل به إذا ذقته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says salsabil and related words describe a drink of exceptional smoothness.
rows.anchor: والسلسل والسلسال: ما كان من الشراب غاية في السلاسة، قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says he had heard the word salsabil nowhere except in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: لم أسمع السلسبيل إلا في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma is a locative adverb denoting distance.
rows.anchor: ثم ظرف مكان للبعد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority consider the surah Meccan; Mujahid and Qatada call it Medinan, while Hasan and ʿIkrima say it is Medinan except the command not to obey a sinner or unbeliever.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول الجمهور. وقال مجاهد وقتادة: مدنية

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
rows.claim: Hasan and ʿIkrima exempt the command ‘do not obey among them a sinner or unbeliever’ as Meccan.
rows.anchor: مدنية إلا آية واحدة فإنها مكية وهي: ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi transmits a view that the surah is Medinan except from ‘be patient for your Lord’s judgment’ onward, which is Meccan.
rows.anchor: حكاه الماوردي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s connection to the previous one is evident and needs no elaboration.
rows.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها ظاهرة جدا لا تحتاج إلى شرح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: They take hal here to mean qad (‘already’), although hal with a nominal clause cannot mean qad and with a verb it usually marks a direct question.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: هي هنا بمعنى قد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation connects hal to an original ahl form with its hamza elided; a poem asking ‘Did they see us?’ is offered as evidence.
rows.anchor: قيل: لأن الأصل أهل، فكأن الهمزة حذفت واجتزئ بها في الاستفهام

rows.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر
rows.claim: When the verse was recited to Abu Bakr, or according to another report Umar, he wished the state of being uncreated and unaccountable had lasted.
rows.anchor: وما تليت عند أبي بكر، وقيل: عند عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال: ليتها تمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The human’ most likely means humanity: the interval is nonexistence or embryonic development through successive stages until a person can be addressed, with no renown during that period.
rows.anchor: والإنسان هنا جنس بني آدم، والحين الذي مر عليه، إما حين عدمه، وإما حين كونه نطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the human as Adam and the interval as the time before his spirit was breathed into him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام، والحين الذي مر عليه هي المدة التي بقي فيها إلى أن نفخ فيه الروح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Adam remained clay for forty years, then shaped clay for forty, then stinking mud for forty, completing his creation in 120 years.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: بقي طينا أربعين سنة، ثم صلصالا أربعين، ثم حمأ مسنونا أربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided humanity by showing the road and the outcomes of guidance and destruction.
rows.anchor: أخبر تعالى أنه هداه إلى السبيل، أي أرشده إلى الطريق

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid says the path is the way to felicity or misery; al-Suddi says it is the route out of the womb.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: سبيل السعادة والشقاوة. وقال السدي: سبيل الخروج من الرحم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God enabled both possibilities and invited people to Islam through rational and transmitted proofs, so belief or unbelief establishes responsibility.
rows.anchor: أي مكناه وأقدرناه في حالتيه جميعا، وإذ دعوناه إلى الإسلام بأدلة العقل والسمع

rows.speaker: أبو السمال وأبو العاج
rows.claim: While most read imma with kasra, Abu al-Sammal and Abu al-ʿAj open both instances, a dialect reported by Abu Zayd and also used as a coordinating particle.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إما بكسر الهمزة فيهما وأبو السمال وأبو العاج

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says gratitude comes by God’s enabling, while ingratitude comes from bad choice.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: إما شاكرا بتوفيقنا، وإما كفورا فبسوء اختياره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shakiran and kafuran are circumstantial phrases from the object pronoun in ‘We guided him’; an alternative makes them describe the two paths metaphorically.
rows.anchor: وانتصب شاكرا وكفورا على الحال من ضمير النصب في هديناه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows the adjectives to qualify the two paths, metaphorically describing them as grateful or ungrateful.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونا حالين من السبيل، أي عرفناه السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shakir is not intensified because gratitude is rare, while kafur is intensified because unbelief is common.
rows.anchor: كان الشكر قل من يتصف به قال شاكرا

rows.speaker: طلحة وعمرو بن عبيد وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة
rows.claim: They read salasil without declension in both pause and continuation; reports differ on pausing with an alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة وعمرو بن عبيد وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة: سلاسل ممنوع الصرف

rows.speaker: حفص وابن ذكوان وباقي السبعة
rows.claim: Hafs and Ibn Dhakwan are reported with nondeclension, while the remaining readers use nunation in continuation and its substitute alif at pause; the author notes dialect and codex evidence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة: بالتنوين وصلا وبالألف المبدلة منه وقفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declined form in a plural is well attested in Arabic; some grammarians even call it optional.
rows.anchor: والصرف في الجمع أتى كثيرا ... حتى ادعى قوم به التخييرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that declension is represented in the codices of Medina, Mecca, Kufa, Basra, Ubayy, and ʿAbd Allah.
rows.anchor: والصرف ثابت في مصاحف المدينة ومكة والكوفة والبصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poetic ending uses n for alif; in singing, the line would otherwise end with the prolongation alif.
rows.anchor: فهذه النون بدل من الألف، إذ لو ترنم لوقف بألف الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Of silver’ means made of silver; kana depicts God bringing the remarkable vessels into being by ‘Be,’ combining silver’s whiteness with glass-like clarity.
rows.anchor: من فضة: أي مخلوقة من فضة، ومعنى كانت: أنه أوجدها تعالى

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads qawarir min fidda in the nominative, as a predicate: ‘they are vessels.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: قوارير من فضة بالرفع، أي هو قرارير

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read qaddaruha actively; its subject may be angels, the attendants, or the blessed recipients.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قدروها مبنيا للفاعل، والضمير للملائكة، أو للطواف عليهم، أو المنعمين

rows.speaker: الربيع ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the vessels are measured to the hands; Mujahid says the drink is measured to satisfy thirst.
rows.anchor: على قدر الأكف، قاله الربيع أو على قدر الري، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the phrase as describing vessels made in each recipient’s desired size and shape; another view says servers portion the drink to thirst so it neither overflows nor falls short.
rows.anchor: أنهم قدروها في أنفسهم على مقادير وأشكال على حسب شهواتهم

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس والسلمي والشعبي وقتادة وزيد بن علي وآخرون
rows.claim: They read the verb passively; Abu ʿAli says the wording implies ‘they were measured out for them,’ with a reversal of the apparent syntax.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي وابن عباس والسلمي والشعبي وابن أبزى وقتادة وزيد بن علي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari derives the passive from a causative sense: God gives them the power to size vessels however they wish.
rows.anchor: ومعناه: جعلوا قادرين لها كما شاءوا، وأطلق لهم أن يقدروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeliest analysis starts with ‘their drink was measured to their thirst from it’; it deletes a noun and then extends the verb to its prepositional object.
rows.anchor: والأقرب في تخريج هذه القراءة الشاذة أن يكون الأصل قدر ريهم منها تقديرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is that ginger flavors the drink, a taste Arabs enjoyed and used in descriptions of women’s breath.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الكأس تمزج بالزنجبيل، والعرب تستلذه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the spring is called ginger because it tastes like ginger.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: تسمى العين زنجبيلا لطعم الزنجبيل فيها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says ginger is the name of a spring in Paradise: the near ones drink it unmixed, while others receive it blended.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الزنجبيل اسم لعين في الجنة، يشرب منها المقربون صرفا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the people of Paradise are served two cups: the first blended with camphor, the second with ginger.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يسقى بجامين، الأول مزاجه الكافور، والثاني مزاجه الزنجبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAynan may replace kaʾsan by ellipsis, replace zanjabil on Qatada’s reading, or be an expression of specification.
rows.anchor: وعينا بدل من كأس على حذف، أي كأس عين، أو من زنجبيل على قول قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salsabil appears to describe a spring whose flow is broad and whose taste is easy; if it were a feminine proper name it would be indeclinable.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه العين تسمى سلسبيلا بمعنى توصف بأنها سلسلة في الاتساع سهلة في المذاق

rows.speaker: طلحة
rows.claim: Talha is reported to read the word without alif, treating it as the spring’s proper name; the majority’s nunation can fit the rhyme and a dialect that declines normally indeclinable words.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن طلحة أنه قرأه بغير ألف، جعله علما لها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says an added b makes the root five letters; the author rejects literal augmentation because b is not a recognized morphological augment.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقد زيدت الباء في التركيب حتى صارت الكلمة خماسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An attribution to Ali that the word commands the Prophet and community to ask for the path to the spring should be removed from tafsir books; the author faults al-Zamakhshari for repeating it.
rows.anchor: ويجب طرحه من كتب التفسير. وأعجب من ذلك توجيه الزمخشري له

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada describes the spring as flowing from beneath the Throne in the Garden of Eden into the other gardens.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: هي عين تنبع من تحت العرش من جنة عدن إلى الجنان

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد ومقاتل
rows.claim: ʿIkrima calls the water sweet and smooth; Mujahid says it flows easily, and Muqatil says it runs through their gathering places as they wish.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: عين سلس ماؤها. وقال مجاهد: عين جديرة الجرية سلسلة سهلة المساغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immortal youths resemble scattered pearls in whiteness, clarity, and their movement about the dwellings in service; a second view compares them to fresh pearls released from their shells.
rows.anchor: وتشبيه الولدان باللؤلؤ المنثور في بياضهم وصفاء ألوانهم وانتشارهم في المساكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to ‘if you see’ is bliss; the omitted object is elided for concision, meaning ‘if you cast your sight there,’ with thumma as an adverb governed by raʾayta.
rows.anchor: وإذا رأيت ما ثم، فحذف ما كما حذف في قوله: لقد تقطع بينكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج والزمخشري
rows.claim: They reject supplying ‘what’ before thumma, since thumma would then be the relative clause’s complement and cannot remain after dropping its antecedent.
rows.anchor: ومن قال معناه ما ثم فقد أخطأ، لأن ثم صلة لما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That prohibition is not agreed upon: Kufa grammarians allow the antecedent to be omitted while its clause remains, as Arabic poetry shows; Ibn ʿAtiyya’s syntactic account is internally flawed.
rows.anchor: وليس بخطأ مجمع عليه، بل قد أجاز ذلك الكوفيون

rows.speaker: الجمهور وحميد الأعرج
rows.claim: The majority read thumma as a locative; Hamid al-Aʿraj reads it as the conjunction ‘then,’ requiring an omitted response to the conditional.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ثم بفتح الثاء وحميد الأعرج: ثم بضم التاء حرف عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘great dominion’ has been explained as seeing God, angels seeking permission to enter, or the breadth of the dwellings; al-Kalbi and Ibn ʿUmar describe even the lowest resident’s immense view and attendants.
rows.anchor: الملك الكبير: اتساع مواضعهم. وقال الكلبي: كبيرا عريضا يبصر أدناهم منزلة

rows.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi the Sage, not the hadith compiler Abu ʿIsa, interprets the dominion as God’s power to create and will what they wish.
rows.anchor: وقال الترمذي، وأظنه الترمذي الحكيم لا أبا عيسى الحافظ صاحب الجامع

rows.speaker: عمر وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد والجحدري وأهل مكة وجمهور السبعة
rows.claim: They read ʿaliyahum with an open ya; other reports include a still ya, a rounded ya, the preposition ʿalayhim, and Aisha’s verb ʿalat-hum.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد والجحدري وأهل مكة وجمهور السبعة: عاليهم بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The several readings allow ‘their garments above them’ as a predicate, as a noun with garments as predicate, or as a prepositional phrase; the open form can be circumstantial from those being served.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالياء مضمومة فمبتدأ خبره ثياب ومن قرأ عليهم حرف جر فثياب مبتدأ

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses the accusative as a circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in ‘are served’ or ‘you thought them,’ or as a description of the people of bliss.
rows.anchor: وعاليهم بالنصب على أنه حال من الضمير في يطوف عليهم
